INLINE_CHECK row — audit's is_superuser heuristic was a false positive (the GET handler has no inline SU branch; SU code lives in sibling POST). Handler is filtered by user_id = caller, so today every authenticated user can list their own. The manifest already defines bam.auth_api_key.list; promote to explicit fastify.requireCan('bam.auth_api_key.list') to bring it in line with the rest of api-key.routes.ts (POST/DELETE/rotate already use dualReadGate).

remove_strategy_notes: internal-helpdesk.routes.ts and internal-llm.routes.ts: already covered by EXCLUDED_PATH_PREFIXES['/internal/']. Their NO_GATE entries appear in the audit only because the generator stamps the file basename WITHOUT the registered mount prefix (the routes are declared as POST /tasks etc but registered with prefix '/internal/helpdesk'). Fix: either teach the generator about server.ts prefix-registration, or add these basenames to a file-level exclusion list to be safe regardless.

auth.routes.ts and oauth.routes.ts: every route in both files is part of the authentication lifecycle (login/register/logout/me/orgs/switch-org/change-password/oauth handshake). Whole-file exclusion is the cleanest rule.

email-verify.routes.ts, public-config.routes.ts, github-webhook.routes.ts, slack-webhook.routes.ts: each file contains only public / token-authed / HMAC-signed endpoints. Whole-file exclusion is correct.
ical.routes.ts: both routes are calendar feed surfaces consumed by external clients. /me/calendar.ics uses ?token=API_KEY custom auth. Whole-file exclusion is correct.

Path-prefix candidates that are partial file matches (need /me/calendar.ics, /projects/:id/calendar.ics, /webhooks/github, /webhooks/slack, /root-redirect, /v1/agents/heartbeat, /v1/guests/accept/, /files/, /public/, /auth/): can be expressed via the prefix list, but the file-based form above is simpler and covers all of them except: GET /root-redirect (in system-settings.routes.ts which still has gated routes), POST /v1/agents/heartbeat (in agent.routes.ts which has other ungated routes), GET /files/* (in upload.routes.ts which has a gated POST /upload), POST /v1/guests/accept/:token (in guest.routes.ts where most routes are gated). For these four, the path-prefix list above is the right tool.

Recommended generator change: add a marker comment convention (// BBB_NO_PERMISSION) that route authors can place on the line above fastify.<verb> calls to opt a single route out without changing the prefix list. This makes future additions self-documenting and avoids hard-coding more paths in the script. The PHASE 1 prefix/file lists above are still needed for the existing routes that pre-date the marker.
anomalies: user.routes.ts:142 and :186 are each claimed by two manifest entries (bam.* and banter.*). The resolver only fires one check per request. Pick a canonical permission_id (likely keep bam.*, drop the banter.* variants from the manifest, since these handlers live in apps/api/src/routes/user.routes.ts) before flipping enforce=on. Tracked in audit §5.1.

bam.file_*.list (upload.routes.ts:121) has a glob-shaped permission_id, which is invalid in the standard catalog format. The manifest generator inferred this from the wildcard path GET /files/*. Recommend renaming to bam.file.download or bam.files.list during the same Phase 1 catalog cleanup.

Audit INLINE_CHECK heuristic mis-flagged api-key.routes.ts:24 (GET /auth/api-keys): the GET handler is plain user-self read with no inline is_superuser branch. The two is_superuser refs in the file are inside POST handlers (lines 71 and 102) that already carry dualReadGate. Classified require_can per the human-curator decision rule.

Generator scope mismatch: the audit lists internal-helpdesk/internal-llm routes as NO_GATE with paths like 'POST /tasks' (declared path) even though server.ts registers them under prefix '/internal/helpdesk' or '/internal/llm'. The audit's is-path-excluded check uses the declared path, not the resolved mount path, so the /internal/ prefix exclusion misses them. Two fixes possible: (a) teach the audit and the generator to compose the registered prefix with the declared path before applying isPathExcluded, OR (b) add the file basenames to a file-level exclusion list. (b) is simpler for Phase 1; (a) is the long-term fix.

agent.routes.ts:67 (POST /v1/agents/heartbeat) was classified REMOVE on the rationale that the MCP convention treats agent_heartbeat as always-permitted core. If the policy team prefers to keep it in the catalog (e.g. so the resolver can log heartbeats with a permission_id), reclassify to shadow_only — the route does run requireAuth + requireServiceKind today, so a SHADOW_ONLY wrapper is non-disruptive.

visibility.routes.ts:36 (POST /v1/visibility/can_access) is similar: it's the universal agent preflight, used by every cross-app agent before posting a citation. Currently classified shadow_only but is a candidate for always-permitted-core status in a follow-up.
